title: Playing on the Capitol and the Piron band excursion boats
summary: Fate Marable's Capitol, the Deluxe, Pichon and Piron bands, and the 1938 breakup.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: I have enough space to quote you word for word. Which boat did you play on? Which of the struck was?

Well, the person I played was Fred Marwell. That was the capital. It was the wooden boat. The capital. Oh, yeah. And they had another boat called Deluxe. I believe it would come down in the summertime. And then after sitting there, they let me go and I went with the Piedhorn band. That was two boats. And Piedhorn had Walter Piedhorn playing piano, and Walter Piedhorn was such a versatile and talented man, so the captain told him, next season you could get your band together and say, we're going to have your band. There was three boats running on the river. And that was the fort around 48. We'd tramp all the way to St. Paul, tramping around them people. And then of course those things were already booked at eight at times, you see.
These were the excursion boats, not the Password? The excursion boats, yeah. Not the Password.

Yeah, excursion boats. Somewhere when I got here in 48, they dropped us off in St. Louis and I was supposed to come back. But Piedhorn went with the band out there and the captain got discouraged. I forgot to repeat that. They had Peter Bocard. And there was a lot of dissension in the band. Peter Bocard was the leader and the Tramble Brothers was supposed to be the manager and they both came over the river and there was a lot of dissension. I could see and feel it. So when I went to Chicago, like I said, the thing was going up and up so much around there and everything. And this buddy I was there, I didn't have much expense, you know. He had a small room for myself and I had wanted to go to Chicago a long time. So the rest of my house stayed there that length of time, see. And the good thing I did, because when the boat came back here, they stopped it all. The war was coming on. They stopped it all right. I was saying I wouldn't allow the fuel. You never did go back to it no more.
